title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.4.5)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.4.5 (2026-11-08)

The web controls follow the permission rules, and a component can move to another dataset. No Grasshopper change: CSC_Update is not needed for this release.

Added

  • Move a component to another dataset: POST /identities/{id}/move and a control in the actions menu of the component, for a moderator of both datasets. One component at a time. A dataset emptied this way can be deleted. Until the nightly run the map may colour a moved component by its old dataset; who sees it is decided at read time (#50).
  • Delete a never-published component: a control with a confirm dialog, for its creator or a moderator (#50).
  • API, open snapshots and corrections: an identity carries has_open_snapshot and an evidence record has_open_correction, for contributors and moderators of the dataset and admins. Only the fact, no details (#47).
  • API, lists of snapshots: GET /snapshots/pending and GET /snapshots?mine=1 carry identity_withdrawn, so the moderation queue and My work hide Publish and Submit there (#49).

Changed

  • Behaviour, a withdrawn component stays out of circulation: reserve, re-enter, undo exit and undo deinstall answer 409 on a withdrawn component. So does adding a photo to a withdrawn snapshot or to any snapshot of a withdrawn component, and adding an attachment to a withdrawn record or to any record of a withdrawn component, and correcting a snapshot of a withdrawn component, and submitting, publishing, promoting or reinstating one, and reinstating an evidence record of it, and withdrawing a snapshot with replacement_id. Recall, reject, back to draft and delete stay, so that an open snapshot can be cleared. A moderator reinstates the component first (#49).
  • Behaviour, revoking an invitation: only a moderator of the dataset, or an admin, revokes an invitation. The creator loses the right with the role (#48).
  • Web, controls the backend allows: a moderator adds an attachment to a published record, and edits the name, notes and date of a withdrawn snapshot, the rest of the form stays disabled there; a contributor reaches their own draft snapshot from the snapshot dialog; a new state, evidence and "out of circulation" stay available when every snapshot is withdrawn; a site admin submits, recalls and returns to draft another person's record; an author edits their evidence draft after losing the contributor role; the layout document of a superseded record can be filled in (#48).
  • Web and backend, wording: user text says "component" for a catalogued component again, also in error messages, the Data Model page and the MCP tool descriptions. 0.6.4.2 had brought in "element", which left the web mixing both words; "element" stays only for the items of a batch. A recorded state is a "snapshot", as in the data model, where the web said "version" in most places; "v1" stays its number.
  • MCP, names: the tools list_versions and get_version are now list_snapshots and get_snapshot; the parameter version_id is snapshot_id, and the answers say snapshots, current_snapshot and snapshot_count. A chat that calls an old name gets "tool not found" once and then sees the new list.
  • Web, page description: the description search engines and link previews show reads "A digital database for reclaimed architectural components."
  • Backend, index: component_snapshots gains an index on identity_id and status, for the check of an open snapshot. It is built when the server starts.

Fixed

  • Web, controls that ended in a refusal: controls the backend would refuse with a 403 or a 409 are hidden, or disabled with the reason, before a form is filled in (#46, #47).
  • Web, claims: a claim with a result saves. The form sent no summary.kind, so the server answered 422 although the form said nothing was missing.
  • Tests: test_signin.py passes on Python 3.9.
  • Backup: pull_production.ps1 passes SSH keepalive options, after a pull of the assets broke at 1.56 GB.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
